items.title: Managing Educational Technology Integration and Teachers’ Digital Literacy in Relation to Student Engagement as Perceived by Teachers in Sagada District
items.abstract: This study aimed to determine the relationship between the management of educational technology by teachers, the digital literacy of teachers, and student engagement in technology-integrated learning through a descriptive-correlational research design. It was found that student engagement in technology-integrated learning, according to teachers’ perceptions, was characterized by an overall mean score of 2.98 on a four-point rating scale, which was interpreted as “Agree,” and that behavioral engagement (M=3.12) and emotional engagement (M=3.14) were both higher compared to cognitive engagement (M=2.67). There was a significant correlation between the teachers’ perception of the management of educational technology integration and student engagement (r=.30, p<.05), while the digital literacy of teachers had a moderate positive correlation with student engagement (r=.42, p<.05). However, student engagement was assessed through teachers’ perceptions rather than direct student reports or classroom observations, which should be considered when interpreting the findings. Based on the results, a comprehensive intervention plan focusing on professional development, collaborative learning communities, technology support, and continuous monitoring was proposed to strengthen technology integration and student engagement in elementary schools.

items.title: Measuring AI-Pedagogical Knowledge in Pre-Service Teachers: Development and Initial Validation of a Vignette-Based Assessment
items.abstract: Abstract : The growing use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in education creates a need for assessments that measure teachers’ pedagogical judgement rather than relying solely on self-reported competence. This study developed and examined initial validity evidence for a vignette-based assessment of AI-pedagogical knowledge among pre-service teachers. Instrument development proceeded from construct definition and blueprinting to an initial pool of 36 researcher-developed vignettes, developer screening, a diagnostic pilot with 60 pre-service teachers, systematic item revision, and content review by three independent experts. The revised 24-item assessment was administered to an analytic sample of 484 pre-service teachers. Validity evidence was examined through expert ratings, internal structure, item and distractor functioning, score reliability and conditional precision, differential item functioning, and relations with external variables. Aiken’s V coefficients ranged from .83 to 1.00 (M = .94), although the small expert panel and restricted use of rating categories warrant cautious interpretation. A one-factor model adequately represented the response data, supporting interpretation of a total score rather than separate domain scores (CFI = .990, TLI = .989, RMSEA = .034, SRMR = .065). Internal consistency was high (KR-20 = .93; categorical omega = .95), but precision was concentrated at the lower end of the ability distribution. Of the participants, 24.2% obtained the maximum score and 47.5% scored 22 or higher. No item showed non-negligible differential functioning by gender or field of study. Knowledge scores were moderately associated with AI self-efficacy (r = .36) and teaching self-efficacy (r = .33) and more weakly associated with self-reported instructional practice (r = .22). The assessment may support formative and research uses when interpreted as a single total score, but it is not yet suitable for ranking or high-stakes decisions. Further development requires more difficult items, revision of weak items and distractors, cognitive interviews, and cross-institutional evaluation.

items.title: Measuring Students’ Attention Boundaries in GAI-Assisted Learning: Development and Validation of the GAI-Mediated Learning Boundary Scale and Latent Profile Analysis
items.abstract: The Generative AI (GAI) is reshaping the temporal and spatial organization of college learning and the perceived boundary crossing between teacher-assigned tasks and self-directed learning. This study developed and validated a scale to assess college students’ attention boundary management in GAI-mediated learning. Analyzing data from 1904 students at 3 colleges in China, the study established a five-dimensional structure: Flexibility, Fragmentation, Immersion, Positive Spillover, and Negative Spillover. Exploratory and Confirmatory Factor Analysis confirmed the scale’s psychometric properties. A Latent Profile Analysis identified four distinct student profiles, Protective, Strained, Overextended, and Engaged Permeability Management. Supplementary heterogeneity analyses examined differences across the four profiles by gender, grade level, university, purposes and duration of AI use, and other learning-related characteristics. Based on these, this study proposed profile-specific recommendations. The study provides a validated instrument for assessing students’ attention boundaries in GAI-mediated learning, identifies heterogeneous student profiles, and offers differentiated practical implications.

items.title: Money Tree: An Open, AI-Assisted Search for Forward-Looking Information in Nominally Random Systems
items.abstract: Money Tree is an ongoing, AI-assisted experimental research program investigating whether reproducible forward-looking information can be detected in chronological systems that are nominally or apparently random. Mega Millions is used as a deliberately difficult experimental target because its outcomes are discrete, chronological, publicly observable, externally generated, and designed to be unpredictable. The objective is not simply to predict lottery numbers. The lottery serves as a stress test for a broader question: can weak forward-looking structure be distinguished from coincidence, false discovery, data leakage, adaptive overfitting, or artifacts created by the way data are represented? The project began in 2026 with a simple historical-frequency question and evolved into a software research laboratory incorporating walk-forward evaluation, matched random controls, Monte Carlo testing, independent analytical engines, falsification procedures, a centralized Referee layer, AI specialist reviews, and prospective high-volume experimentation. This research is being released while it is still in progress. No claim of reliable lottery prediction is made. Positive, negative, inconclusive, and failed experiments are intentionally preserved in the research record. Collaboration is a primary purpose of this release. We welcome researchers, independent investigators, mathematicians, statisticians, software developers, and others working with stochastic processes, sequential prediction, complex systems, information theory, experimental mathematics, random-number testing, anomaly detection, or other noisy chronological systems. We are particularly interested in people who have methods, datasets, criticisms, or ongoing experiments that could independently challenge this framework. We are also interested in helping evaluate outside experiments or datasets where our developing zero-trust, walk-forward, matched-control methodology may be useful. A rigorous demonstration that one of our ideas is wrong is considered a successful contribution. The project was initiated and directed by Troy Stuart, who began without a computer-programming or computer-science background and learned AI prompting, Python development workflows, Visual Studio Code, GitHub, version control, testing, and experimental research practices while building the project step by step. ChatGPT, known throughout the project as “Chappie,” has served as a substantive AI research collaborator in research framing, discussion, drafting, code-oriented guidance, critique, documentation, and coordination of independent AI specialist reviews. Troy Stuart remains the human project originator, decision-maker, and accountable author. Research status: Ongoing.Version: 1.0Release date: October 2, 2026.

items.title: Multicenter, Multivendor Development and Validation of Automated Liver Prescription
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Manual prescription of liver MRI volumes introduces inter‐operator variability and prolongs exam duration. Artificial intelligence (AI)‐based prescription has been demonstrated, but existing work has been limited to single‐vendor settings. Purpose To develop and validate an AI model for automated liver MRI prescription using a large, consecutive, multicenter dataset encompassing multiple vendors, field strengths, localizer sequences, and liver pathologies. Study Type Retrospective. Population A total of 11,012 patients (5928 female) who underwent liver MRI exams across three vendors (GE HealthCare, Philips Healthcare, Siemens Healthineers) at three institutions, split into training/validation/test sets (70/10/20%). Liver disorders included cirrhosis, ascites, portal hypertension, and iron overload. Field Strength/Sequence Three‐plane localizers acquired using single‐shot fast spin echo (68.3%) and gradient echo (31.7%) at 1.5 T (52.8%) and 3 T (47.2%). Assessment A YOLOv8 object detection model was trained to detect the liver, torso, and arms on localizer images. Automated prescription accuracy was assessed using three‐dimensional intersection‐over‐union (IoU 3D ) for axial, coronal, and sagittal prescriptions. Subgroup analyses evaluated performance across technical and patient‐related factors. Statistical Tests Mann–Whitney U tests with Bonferroni correction, Kruskal‐Wallis tests, Wilcoxon signed‐rank tests, Spearman correlation. Effect sizes were calculated using rank‐biserial correlation ( r rb ) and epsilon‐squared ( ε 2 ). p < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results Median axial prescription IoU 3D was 0.963 (interquartile range: 0.946–0.976), with median IoU 3D above 0.940 for coronal and sagittal prescriptions. For axial prescriptions, margins less than 4 mm in each direction were required to achieve complete coverage of manual prescriptions in 90% of cases in the held‐out test set. Effects were negligible to small across vendors, field strengths, localizer sequences, and patient factors ( r rb ≤ 0.16, ε 2 ≤ 0.01). Data Conclusion A single multivendor model achieved accurate automated liver MRI prescription without clinically meaningful performance differences across vendors, field strengths, localizer sequences, or patient factors. Evidence Level 2. Technical Efficacy Stage 1.

items.title: Muslim: A Deployed Arabic Voice AI Platform for Grounded Islamic Knowledge
items.abstract: We present Muslim, a production Arabic voice AI platform serving grounded, sourced Islamic knowledge to real users. Beyond a real-time voice pipeline (NeMo Arabic ASR, an OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint, self-hosted TTS) and a deterministic multi-source retrieval layer routed across six Model Context Protocol servers, we report three things a research prototype typically lacks. First, a released family of fine-tuned Arabic Islamic model artifacts: an efficient tool-routing LLM (Muslim-6B-PRO, 5.94B parameters) and a Modern Standard Arabic TTS model (Fasih-TTS-V1) that ranks 5th of 17 overall and 2nd of 11 open-weight systems on the community-voted Arabic TTS Arena for MSA. Second, an account and metering layer - a free per-account turn allowance, capacity-aware refusal, and email verification deferred to the point it actually matters - that turns an open demo into an operable, abuse-resistant product. Third, a three-layer observability stack (liveness, error reporting, product analytics) built specifically around the system's characteristic failure mode: a GPU-bound agent host going silent while the web tier keeps serving normally. We report real, measured latency and accuracy figures (98.4% recitation-validation accuracy on 124 cases; end-to-end voice latency of 0.9-1.7s) and discuss the concrete engineering trade-offs and limitations of running an Islamic-knowledge voice product in production.

items.title: Natural Zeolite Concrete Under Acidic and Sulphate Environments: A Comprehensive Review
items.abstract: This review evaluates the performance of natural-zeolite concrete under acidic and sulfate attack. The review discusses the literature on visual deterioration, weight loss, erosion depth, compressive strength retention, service life, and microstructural characteristics. The findings indicate that the durability performance of natural-zeolite concrete depends on the type of aggressive environment and the zeolite replacement level. Under sulfate exposure, natural zeolite improves durability by consuming calcium hydroxide and promoting the formation of additional calcium silicate hydrate (C-S-H) . It also reduces gypsum and ettringite formation, which improves compressive strength retention and extends the service life of concrete. One study showed that 20% zeolite extended service life from 15 to 35 months and maintained more than 75% relative compressive strength after 1050 days of sodium sulfate exposure. The results are study-specific and should not be considered a universal optimum. In contrast, the reported performance under sulfuric acid attack remains inconsistent. However, higher replacement levels (15%–30%) have also been associated with increased surface deterioration and strength loss under severe acid exposure. The review demonstrates that sulfuric acid is more aggressive than hydrochloric acid. However, differences in acid concentration, pH, exposure duration, and solution renewal limit direct comparison. The review also highlights that combining zeolite with tuff can partially mitigate tuff's adverse effects under acidic conditions. In addition, recent advances in artificial intelligence and machine learning demonstrate considerable potential for predicting and optimizing the performance of zeolite concrete by capturing nonlinear relationships. However, applying AI-based approaches to predict sulfuric-acid-induced deterioration and the sulfate resistance of natural-zeolite concrete remains largely unexplored. Conflicting findings among available studies also highlight the need for systematic investigations to establish the optimum zeolite replacement level and identify the governing parameters responsible for variations.

items.title: Occupational Health and Safety in Zambia
items.abstract: The state of occupational health and safety (OH&S) in Zambia, particularly focusing on small-scale contractors (SSCs), is presented in this chapter, highlighting the country’s economic and labour context and the role of SSCs in the creation of employment and delivery of infrastructure despite limited finance and technical capacity. A review on the registration and grading process under the National Council for Construction is presented with a view to outlining that most SSCs in Zambia that operate in lower grades experience restricted access to high-value contracts, which often results in subcontracting with other capable, larger companies. An analysis of the legal and regulatory framework that establishes employers’ and employees’ duties and responsibilities, compensation mechanisms, and environmental safeguards and their enforcement, which remain inconsistent, has been outlined. The chapter highlights a critical OH&S Policy established under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 16 of 2025 that enables employers to ensure that the working environments are safe and to undertake health risk assessments. Gaps in the legal framework are that their complexity leads to failure to comply by SSCs in terms of inadequate awareness and training, limited access to OH&S services, especially for the SSCs working in rural Zambia, and a lack of technical skills. Zambia, on one hand, has ratified some of the International Labour Organisation (ILO) conventions that also contribute to the OH&S oversight, thus showing willingness to improve the safety and health of workplaces by this recognition of global standards.

items.title: Occupational Health and Safety Performance Management Issues in Developing Countries
items.abstract: In this chapter, focused representative cases were selected to explore occupational health and safety (OH&S) performance management in developing countries, Ghana, and South Africa. Although these countries possess unique systems, they share common problems that crosscut small-scale contractors (SSCs) in industries like energy, oil, gas, and construction where these contractors dominate but have inadequate capacity to effectively manage OH&S. Elevated accidents, injuries and fatality are recorded attributable to inadequate skills, weak communication systems, insufficient regulatory compliance, corruption, and limited resources, which collectively lead to under-reporting of incidents, hindering effective implementation of interventions. While globalisation and rapid industrialisation add to the risks, the inherited legal systems, fragmented policies, and inadequate institutional capacity have continued to direct OH&S systems. The chapter expounds on how Ghana has illustrated progress in line with the development of legislative initiatives for SSCs, with no coherent OH&S policy. South Africa reflects a more robust legal framework while encountering enforcement gaps. The International Labour Organisation (ILO) conventions and the Southern African Development Community (SADCC) convention are informing regional initiatives on the significance of streamlined OH&S standards, improved collection of data, and improved cooperation among stakeholders. This chapter underscores the development of an integrated framework that supports awareness, training, and reduced incidents to ensure workers’ safety. Sub-Saharan African countries, including Zambia, can operationalise lessons to develop OH&S initiatives for safer, sustainable workplaces.

items.title: Occupational Health and Safety Performance Management, Measurements, Framework Dimensions, and Metrics
items.abstract: In recent years, occupational health and safety (OH&S) performance management has been gaining recognition as an important driver in attaining sustainable development with the view of assisting small-scale contractors (SSCs) who are in environments that are resource-strained. Therefore, this chapter analyses the OH&S performance management conceptual perspective relationship with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the process of measurement, indicators to be adopted, and the frameworks. Evidently, inadequate OH&S exposes employees to hazardous conditions that lead to reduced productivity and eventually reinforce poverty. Conversely, this chapter illustrates how effective OH&S performance management supports SDGs 1, 3, and 8 on poverty reduction, health and well-being, and decent work and economic growth, respectively, by highlighting the significance of OH&S measurement through outcome indicators and positive performance indicators (PPIs). These outcomes and indicators promote audits, identification of hazards, and assessment of safety culture. By incorporating PPIs with outcome indicators, continuous improvement, safety at the workplace, and well-being for employees can be achieved. Ultimately, this chapter reinforces that resilient OH&S performance management is fundamental in ensuring that the workers are safe by reducing the rate of accidents and fostering sustainable economic growth.

items.title: Occupational Health and Safety Risk Analysis of Six Engineering Laboratories Using an Activity-Based HIRARC Approach
items.abstract: Engineering laboratories combine high-energy machinery, live circuits, pressurised fluids and open flames with novice student operators, yet occupational health and safety in Indonesian higher education is still managed largely through academic rather than risk-based instruments. This study applies Hazard Identification, Risk Assessment and Risk Control (HIRARC) to six practicum laboratories of the Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering, Universitas Tidar, using the practicum activity rather than the room as the unit of analysis. Hazards were identified through direct observation and document review and scored by an assessor panel on a 5 x 5 matrix with predefined severity and likelihood criteria. Three main findings emerge. First, the 27 activity-level hazards are dominated by mechanical sources, and nearly half of the activities (44%) are high risk before control. Second, risk profiles differ between laboratories: the machining-intensive Production Process, Welding and CNC laboratories carry the highest mean risk, while the single most severe activity is CNC operation with a running spindle, so mean-based and peak-based rankings point to different priorities. Third, combined engineering and administrative controls, each mapped to the Indonesian regulation that requires it, are expected by the assessor panel to bring every activity to the low band, an estimated mean reduction of 58.5%; this is a prospective panel estimate, not a result measured after implementation. The study contributes an activity-based, regulation-linked risk register that allows laboratories with different energy profiles to be compared on one scale and to be prioritised for safety investment.

items.title: On AI-augmented transformatizing in practice: protocols, quality criteria, and reporting standards for Human-AI Augmented Mixed Methods Research
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly reshaping qualitative research, quantitative research, and mixed methods research, but practical guidance for conducting, evaluating, and reporting human–AI analytic collaboration remains underdeveloped. Building on AI-augmented transformatizing, a representational–recursive framework that conceptualizes AI as a participant in analytic re-representation rather than merely as a technical tool, this article advances a practice-oriented framework for Human-AI Augmented Mixed Methods Research. The article offers three integrated contributions. First, it proposes the AI-Augmented Transformatizing Protocol , a recursive workflow for preparing representations, for assigning human and AI analytic roles, for generating AI-assisted transformations, for conducting human critique, for refining findings, and for constructing meta-inferences. Second, it introduces quality criteria for assessing methodological rigor in human-AI augmented analysis, including representational fidelity, prompt traceability, recursive transparency, human oversight integrity, algorithmic reflexivity, convergence-divergence interrogation, meta-inferential robustness, and ethical accountability. Third, it presents reporting standards designed to help authors disclose AI systems, model versions, prompting procedures, analytic iterations, researcher interventions, validation/legitimation strategies, ethical safeguards, and limitations. These proposed methodological components are conceptual and practice-oriented rather than empirically validated; accordingly, the worked example illustrates their operational logic, whereas future research is needed to establish their empirical performance, including the validity and reliability of the HAAM-QAM. Rather than treating AI use as an optional efficiency enhancement, the framework positions human-AI collaboration as a structured methodological practice requiring explicit design, documentation, reflexivity, and accountability. By translating the theory of AI-augmented transformatizing into protocols, quality criteria, and reporting standards, this article provides methodologists, researchers, authors, reviewers, editors, graduate educators, mentors, and the like with practical guidance for conducting transparent, rigorous, and ethically responsible AI-augmented mixed methods research in psychology and related fields. In so doing, it extends current reporting guidelines and quality frameworks by addressing the distinctive representational, recursive, and ethical demands introduced when AI participates directly in analysis.

items.title: Patient-Centered Observations of Outpatient Hemodialysis: An Exploratory Systems Approach to Understanding Infection Prevention Using Human Factors.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Infection remains the second leading cause of death in patients with ESKD on hemodialysis. This exploratory analysis sought to characterize interruptions and non-routine events (NREs), in the outpatient dialysis setting, with particular interest in the relationships between interruptions and NREs and infection prevention and control (IPC) activities. METHODS: We conducted a mixed-methods, observational, exploratory study of 45 patients and their dialysis teams across four U.S. dialysis facilities (99 total outpatient hemodialysis treatments hours observed). Structured observations were focused on the team surrounding an individual patient for the duration of their dialysis session using a modified Line Operations Safety Audit (LOSA) approach. Quantitative analyses were conducted. RESULTS: A technician simultaneously caring for four patients can experience a median of 64 interruptions, or 16 per patient (range 3-50) during their treatment time. The phases with greatest risk of infection (i.e., connection, disconnection) had a significantly higher time required to complete (with NRE: connection 14:37, disconnection 13:41; without NRE: connection 7:32, disconnection 8:18). Thirty-seven of 45 patients experienced at least one NRE during clinical care, defined as a patient-related clinical event (e.g., long clotting time) or an operational variation (e.g., transportation problem). Findings are exploratory in nature and provide support for future hypothesis generation and testing. CONCLUSIONS: Interruptions and NREs were frequent in the outpatient dialysis work system, and connection and disconnection times were longer when an NRE was present. Since these disruptions occurred during phases that include IPC-related activities, they may introduce competing demands that could challenge consistent adherence, though adherence was not directly measured. These exploratory findings may inform the design of workflows and processes that better support IPC and patient safety in the outpatient dialysis setting.

items.title: PENGARUH PENGGUNAAN AI GENERATIF TERHADAP KEMANDIRIAN BELAJAR MAHASISWA GENERASI Z
items.abstract: This study aims to analyze the influence of Generative AI usage on the learning independence of Generation Z students at STIT Darul Ulum Kotabaru, viewed from the perspective of perceived ease of use and potential dependency. The research employs a quantitative approach with an associative causal design. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to Generation Z students who have used Generative AI in academic activities. The variables examined include perceived ease of use of Generative AI (X1), potential dependency on Generative AI (X2), and student learning independence (Y). Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression with SPSS. The results indicate that perceived ease of use and potential dependency simultaneously influence students' learning independence. Generative AI provides significant convenience in accessing information, understanding materials, and completing academic tasks. However, excessive use without critical thinking and academic responsibility can lead to dependency that reduces learning independence. This study contributes to the development of educational technology studies, particularly in understanding the impact of Generative AI on student learning behavior in Islamic higher education institutions

items.title: Perbandingan Decision Tree dan Random Forest untuk Deteksi Dini Diabetes
items.abstract: Diabetes mellitus merupakan gangguan metabolik kronis yang membutuhkan deteksi dini agar komplikasi jangka panjang dapat dicegah sejak awal. Penelitian ini membandingkan kinerja prediktif dua algoritma klasifikasi berbasis pohon, yaitu Decision Tree dan Random Forest, dalam mendeteksi diabetes pada tahap awal menggunakan dataset Pima Indians Diabetes dari UCI Machine Learning Repository. Sebagai pelengkap, penelitian ini juga menerapkan kerangka Explainable Artificial Intelligence lima lapis yang memanfaatkan SHAP guna menghasilkan penjelasan model yang relevan secara klinis, mulai dari kepentingan fitur global hingga validasi terhadap pengetahuan patofisiologi. Rekayasa fitur dilakukan untuk memperluas ruang fitur dari 8 menjadi 14 variabel, sementara tahap praproses meliputi stratified train-test split, imputasi median, winsorizing berbasis IQR, normalisasi Min-Max, dan SMOTE untuk menyeimbangkan distribusi kelas yang tidak proporsional. Optimasi hyperparameter dilakukan melalui GridSearchCV dengan Stratified K-Fold sebanyak lima lipatan, menggunakan F1-Score sebagai kriteria utama. Hasil eksperimen menunjukkan bahwa Random Forest secara konsisten mengungguli Decision Tree pada seluruh metrik evaluasi, dengan F1-Score cross-validation sebesar 0,9002 berbanding 0,8687 dan ROC-AUC pada set pengujian sebesar 80,61% berbanding 70,43%. McNemar Test menunjukkan bahwa perbedaan pola kesalahan klasifikasi antar kedua model tidak signifikan secara statistik pada ukuran sampel yang tersedia, namun pertimbangan multidimensional seperti stabilitas cross-validation dan selisih ROC-AUC tetap mendukung rekomendasi terhadap Random Forest. Analisis SHAP mengonfirmasi bahwa Insulin, Glucose, dan rasio Insulin terhadap Glucose merupakan tiga prediktor paling berpengaruh, sejalan dengan mekanisme patofisiologi diabetes tipe 2 yang telah mapan dalam literatur kedokteran. Penelitian ini juga mengakui keterbatasan generalisabilitas dataset terhadap populasi Indonesia sebagai catatan penting bagi penelitian lanjutan.

items.abstract: In this article, I aim to analyze the perceptions and uses of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) among students at Higher Education Institutes (HEIs) in Salta. Through a mixed-methods approach based on surveys, it investigates the tension between the massive student adoption for autonomous learning and the infrastructural shortcomings that deepen the digital divide in a local context. The obtained sample evidences a predominant enthusiasm for the emancipatory potential of GenAI, although ethical concerns persist regarding data reliability and the fear of replacing the teaching role. It is observed that the appropriation of AI occurs mostly in a delocalized manner and without pedagogical support, highlighting the urgency to update teacher training while also promoting public policies that guarantee a critical and inclusive integration.

items.title: Perceptions of ChatGPT- and veterinarian-generated responses to pet owners’ medical questions
items.abstract: Background Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming increasingly significant in veterinary medicine, particularly in answering pet owners’ medical questions. AI’s integration could reduce veterinary professionals’ workload while improving access to medical advice. However, the reliability and quality of AI-generated responses compared to veterinarians’ remain unexplored. The objective was to determine whether AI-generated responses were perceived as comparable to veterinarian-generated responses. Methods This cross-sectional study analysed the answers to a sample of pet owners’ medical questions. Both a veterinarian and ChatGPT (GPT-4o, May 2024) provided answers, which were anonymised and presented in a survey distributed through mailing lists and public Facebook groups. Participants were asked to assess each response based on structure, quality, and empathy, using a five-point Likert scale. They then had to indicate whether they trusted the response, and which response they preferred. Results Over two-thirds of the 201 participants (68%) preferred the ChatGPT-generated answers ( p < 0.05), which were rated higher in structure, quality, and empathy. Limitations This study has several limitations, including a small sample size, reliance on a single veterinarian, and use of only two Reddit-derived scenarios. Response accuracy was not assessed, and word count restrictions may have affected perceived response quality. Additionally, prior research suggests that irrelevant patient details can impact ChatGPT’s accuracy, raising questions about user trust if clinical inaccuracies were present. Conclusion AI-generated responses received higher participant ratings in structure, quality and empathy, suggesting AI may enhance veterinary client communication when used under appropriate professional supervision.

items.title: Perspectives on inverse design for AI magnonics
items.abstract: Abstract Inverse design - specifying a desired functionality and letting a computational algorithm search for a structure that meets it - has emerged as a powerful paradigm for magnonic device engineering. In this article, we survey the rapidly growing field of inverse-design magnonics, organising it along two axes: the design variables (topology, material parameters, and magnetic field landscape) and the algorithmic toolbox (gradient-free, gradient-based, and neural-network-based methods) together with the differentiable micromagnetic solvers that enable them. We then identify open frontiers that we consider most promising for the next phase of the field: sensitivity analysis and robust design to bridge the gap between simulation and experiment; input shaping and transducer optimisation; the incorporation of nonlinear spin-wave effects as an explicit design resource; spatially structured amplification; self-adapting media and machine-learning-based design; and the long-term vision of a universal, reconfigurable magnonic platform. We argue that magnonics and artificial intelligence are converging from two directions-machine-learning tools for designing magnonic devices, and magnonic devices as hardware for neuromorphic computation-and propose the term AI magnonics to describe this emerging paradigm.

items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, is fundamentally transforming academic work in higher education, reshaping teaching, research, data analysis, scholarly writing, and the resolution of increasingly complex academic tasks. Nevertheless, access to and use of AI does not automatically translate into effective AI-enabled academic capability. The gap between merely “using AI” and developing meaningful human–AI collaboration has therefore emerged as a critical issue in contemporary faculty development. This study aims to identify and empirically examine the factors shaping lecturers’ competence in effectively leveraging AI to address complex academic tasks in non-public universities in Vietnam. Particular attention is given to the roles of AI literacy, AI self-efficacy, Human–AI Collaboration Competence, and critical AI use, while examining institutional AI support as a potential moderating mechanism. A sequential mixed-methods design is proposed. The qualitative phase employs expert interviews and/or a Delphi process to develop, refine, and validate the conceptual dimensions and measurement indicators. The quantitative phase involves a large-scale survey of lecturers working in Vietnamese non-public universities. Structural equation modelling, using PLS-SEM or CB-SEM depending on data characteristics and model specifications, is employed to examine direct, mediating, and moderating relationships among the proposed constructs. The study is designed to identify the mechanisms through which AI literacy and AI self-efficacy are transformed into Human–AI Collaboration Competence, Critical AI Use, and AI-Enabled Academic Task Competence, ultimately contributing to lecturers’ capacity to perform complex academic tasks effectively. The proposed model provides an integrated explanation of how individual capabilities and institutional conditions jointly shape AI-enabled academic performance. The study proposes an AI-Enabled Academic Capability Development Model as a conceptual and empirical foundation for faculty development in the global digital era. The findings are expected to provide practical implications for non-public universities in designing AI competency development programmes, strengthening institutional AI support ecosystems, and promoting critical, responsible, and academically productive human–AI collaboration.

items.title: Physiological activation regimes reveal distinct autonomic mechanisms underlying operational performance under cognitive workload and stress
items.abstract: Human performance in safety-critical environments depends on the interaction between mental workload, stress, autonomic regulation, and behavior. This study investigated whether associations between heart rate variability (HRV) and performance varied across physiological activation ranges and operational contexts during a multi-task flight simulation implemented through the AeroStim platform. Forty-two healthy participants (25 ± 5 years) performed either a Workload-Only condition (WO; n = 20), comprising Tracking and System Monitoring tasks, or a Stress-Oriented condition (SO; n = 22), in which additional stress-inducing tasks were concurrently administered. ECG was continuously recorded using an EqVital wearable T-shirt. Linear and non-linear HRV indices were extracted and normalized within participants using Min-Max scaling. Gaussian Mixture Modeling of normalized SDNN identified three relative, subject-specific activation ranges ( Easy, Medium , and Hard ), with classification showing high stability across alternative normalization procedures. HRV-performance associations were assessed using Spearman correlations with permutation-based inference and Benjamini–Hochberg correction, while performance differences were evaluated using non-parametric tests. HRV-performance correlations varied across activation ranges and contexts; none passed FDR correction, so these should be considered exploratory. In WO, associations involved LF in the Easy range, SDNN, SD2, and LF in the Medium range, and SDNN, LF/HF, and Sample Entropy in the Hard range. In SO, associations in the Medium range extended to vagal, global variability, and non-linear complexity indices, while Hard-range associations mainly involved vagal and LF-related measures. Omission rate was lower at Medium than Easy activation in WO, providing partial support for an intermediate activation advantage, whereas no consistent performance optimum emerged across contexts. Between-condition comparisons revealed a robust speed-accuracy trade-off, with WO producing faster but less accurate responses and SO producing slower but more accurate responses. Sensitivity analysis further indicated that differences in exercise windows affected HRV metrics in a metric-dependent manner, with greater deviations generally observed for frequency-domain measures. The findings suggest that HRV-performance relationships are context- and activation-dependent rather than captured by a single universal marker. The results support the potential of regime-based, multimodal HRV monitoring for adaptive human-machine systems, while highlighting the need for standardized recording durations, independent autonomic markers, and validation across individuals and real operational environments.

items.title: Precision Pharmacotherapy in Vitiligo
items.abstract: Precision pharmacotherapy is a paradigm shift in managing vitiligo that has shifted from a one size fits all approach to a stratified, mechanism based approach. This chapter introduces an integrated approach addressing clinical phenotype, immune endotype, and therapeutic mechanism to maximize the use of both topical and systemic, as well as targeted Janus kinase inhibitors. Potency-stratified topicals, pulse systemic immunomodulators and selective JAK1 or JAK1/JAK2 or JAK3/TEC inhibitors fit into a step-up algorithm based on disease activity, anatomical location, age and comorbidity. The discussion highlights emerging enablers like lesion mapping using artificial intelligence, digital phenotyping, digital twins, and pharmacogenomic prediction as tools for response prediction on extent scoring and decision support for durable, personalized repigmentation with balanced safety.

items.title: Predicting Faults in Mechanical Systems Using Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
items.abstract: The occurrence of unexpected malfunctions of mechanical systems such as bearings, gearboxes, turbofan engines, and other rotating machinery is still the main cause of downtime, safety hazards, and maintenance cost throughout the manufacturing, energy, and transportation sectors. Recent technological advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) technology have transformed fault prediction from an entirely physics-based activity to a data-based activity, in which sensors, signal processing, and learning algorithms estimate the health state of a machine together. This paper provides a structured assessment and comparative synthesis of AI/ML fault-prediction literature. Nineteen peer-reviewed studies obtained from scholarly and web-based databases for the period 2011–2026 are reviewed. A review of the two main tasks: fault diagnosis – classification of fault type, location and severity – prognosis – prediction of remaining useful life, RUL. The evidence is structured into a six-stage pipeline – data acquisition, pre-processing, feature extraction, model training, output, maintenance decision. The analysis is conducted using various test rigs including the CWRU bearings as well as NASA C-MAPSS turbofan engines and gearbox. The results show that on these benchmarks, convolutional and recurrent deep architectures, attention-augmented LSTMs, and ensemble methods consistently outperform classical classifiers; root-mean-square errors (RMSE) on C-MAPSS RUL errors are about 12 cycles and classification accuracies on CWRU exceed 98%. Simultaneously, the review also outlines a number of ongoing open challenges, like data scarcity, domain shift, class imbalance, limited interpretability, and overoptimistic evaluation, which must be overcome before lab results can become consistent with the reliable deployment in the industry. To conclude the paper suggests a standardized benchmarking of multi-fidelity methodologies and explainability-augmented models.

items.title: Preregistration of the Expert-Panel Analysis Plan: LLMs as Pre-Administration Item Reviewers in Programming Education
items.abstract: This record preregisters the analysis plan for the expert-panel component of a study comparing large language model (LLM) item reviews with classical item analysis for a 60-item multiple-choice C# programming achievement test (associate degree, Türkiye). The plan was registered before any expert response was collected. Classical item analysis (N = 150 students) and blind LLM evaluations (Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol, DeepSeek V4 Pro; two rounds each) were completed before registration and are not part of the preregistered analyses. The plan specifies content-validity indices (I-CVI, modified kappa, S-CVI), inter-rater consistency measures, comparisons of expert judgements with LLM judgements and empirical indices, expert versus LLM accuracy in predicting the most attractive distractor, and a triangulation-based item-selection protocol. Item texts are not shared for test-security reasons. Version 1.1 (2 October 2026) adds an amendment registered before any expert response was received: panel of four experts; exclusion of an AI-generated pilot response from the preregistered analyses; and a sensitivity analysis by programming background. The primary analyses are unchanged.

items.title: Preserving traditional plant knowledge via AI-driven identification and human-centered mobile design
items.abstract: The loss of indigenous botanical knowledge poses risks to biodiversity conservation and community health by weakening the knowledge of medicinal plants and their traditional use as local plant-based health care options. An integrated system that combines deep learning image recognition with a user-friendly mobile interface to document and preserve medicinal plant knowledge is presented in this study. A Convolutional neural network (CNN) was trained on a curated dataset of fourteen Nigerian medicinal plants, achieving 78.9% validation accuracy in species identification. Recognized plants are linked to an expert-curated knowledge base (with features, compounds, and uses) structured as a graph for efficient retrieval. A mobile app prototype was also designed with intuitive user interfaces, such as a landing page for navigation and an image-based search screen for plant identification. The Human-Computer Interaction (HCI)-driven design emphasizes ease-of-use, with clear labels and minimal steps, enabling users (including elders and youth) to capture plant images and instantly access scientific and local names, medicinal properties, and usage guidelines. In “active learning” mode, low-confidence predictions trigger the retrieval of similar examples to guide users. This Artificial Intelligence plus Human-Computer Interaction approach addresses issues of manual identification (subjectivity, expertise gap) by automating recognition and by empowering communities to digitally record ethnobotanical knowledge. By improving accessibility to reliable plant data, this system contributes to Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) 3 and 15.

items.title: Priority-Weighted System Dynamics for Cost-Effective Risk Mitigation in High-Risk Storage Facilities
items.abstract: High-risk storage facilities function as sociotechnical systems in which technical reliability, human performance, organizational control, and environmental stress interact over time, so their risk cannot be captured by a single probability-impact score. This study develops a priority-weighted System Dynamics model to evaluate risk mitigation strategies prior to implementation, using ammunition storage as the empirical case. Analytic Network Process (ANP) weights, validated through a Fuzzy Delphi panel, are embedded directly in the stock-flow structure so that the relative importance of interdependent risk factors shapes how risk evolves under each policy. Over a 60-month horizon, the baseline raised the Total Risk Index (TRI) from 29.65 to 44.57, whereas full implementation of the prioritized mitigation set lowered it to 14.88. items.title: Process-oriented approach to anti-crisis management of an enterprise
items.abstract: In the modern conditions of the market economy, the organization is characterized by a functional approach to enterprise management. However, the frequent occurrence of crisis phenomena has shown that this approach is too cumbersome and does not allow for timely response to negative conditions. A more flexible approach is needed to manage the organization more effectively. Thus, the process approach is more appropriate, with its help it is possible to develop and optimize various business processes and optimize the whole process in general. The use of a process approach minimizes the impact of the human factor, reduces costs, increases flexibility and speed of management decision-making, and allows for timely response to changes in the external and internal environment. This approach is relevant and serves as an effective solution and prevention method for crisis situations.

items.title: Prompt-as-a-Protocol with Agentic Research Automation: A Validated Methodology for AI-Native Biomedical Data Science Producing Peer-Reviewed Findings Across Genomics and Biosensor Domains
items.abstract: Recent advances in large language model (LLM)-driven agentic systems have demonstrated capabilities for automating biomedical data analysis workflows. However, existing systems are predominantly validated on synthetic benchmarks or retrospective tasks, without demonstrated production of novel, peer-reviewed biological findings. Here we describe Prompt-as-a-Protocol (PaaP), a methodology that converts natural-language research questions into structured, executable analytical protocols, coupled with an agentic Generative Research Automation (GRA) layer that executes these protocols with integrated quality assurance. We validate PaaP+GRA through two prospective case studies in distinct biomedical domains. In single-cell transcriptomics, the pipeline identified KIF3A as the sole genome-wide significant correlate of ciliation status in human striatal parvalbumin interneurons (adjusted p = 1.37 x 10-14), while autonomously detecting and correcting a sex composition confound (p = 8.1 x 10-44) that would have produced spurious results. In biosensor analytics, the pipeline achieved calibrated PPG-to-ECG heart rate variability classification matching gold-standard ECG performance (ROC AUC = 0.85) for stress-state discrimination relevant to alcohol use disorder relapse monitoring. Both studies have been submitted for peer review. To our knowledge, PaaP+GRA is the first prompt-to-protocol methodology validated by prospective production of novel biological findings across multiple domains, including autonomous confound detection, rather than benchmark performance alone.

items.title: Protecting Trademark in the Metaverse: The Emerging Threat of AI-Generated Counterfeits
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence tools allow metaverse users to generate virtual wearables, avatar accessories and other branded goods, which often infringe upon trademark rights. These infringing goods, however, are not static counterfeits but dynamically generated knockoffs that rarely explicitly name the trademark owner and take place in novel digital environments. This paper analyses whether and how Indian trademark laws can tackle such emerging forms of infringement based on the doctrine of “use in the course of trade”, the “identical or similar goods” jurisdictional anchor and the “likelihood of confusion” standard. It argues that the ability of Indian trademark law to address these concerns is limited by the very existence of doctrines and tests that seek to make sense of trademark infringement in virtual settings, as well as the lack of a holistic regulatory approach to the liability of metaverse platforms under the Trade Marks Act, 1999 and the Information Technology Act, 2000. By relying on recent Indian, EU, US and UK jurisprudence and early cases on trademarks and AI-generated counterfeits, the paper highlights the jurisdictional fragmentation in addressing generative AI infringement in India and proposes a unified approach to enforcing trademark rights against dynamically generated virtual counterfeits.

items.title: Psychological Outcomes and Correlates Associated with Over-Reliance on Artificial Intelligence Tools: An Integrative Review
items.abstract: Abstract The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) has raised concerns about over-reliance and its psychological implications. This integrative review synthesised psychological outcomes and correlates associated with AI over-reliance and examined its conceptualisation and measurement. The review included 28 studies identified through database and citation searching. AI over-reliance was associated with depression, anxiety, psychological distress, and cognitive disengagement, while findings concerning well-being and self-related functioning, including self-efficacy and autonomy, were mixed and context-dependent. Evidence concerning social or relational functioning was particularly limited, with only one included study directly examining this domain as an outcome. Most evidence was cross-sectional and therefore did not establish temporal direction or causality. Notably, the only longitudinal study found that depression and anxiety predicted subsequent AI dependence, whereas dependence did not predict later depression or anxiety, suggesting that psychological distress may precede dependence. No consensus definition or measure emerged; studies examined reliance, psychological dependence, problematic or compulsive use, and addiction-like engagement. AI over-reliance is therefore best understood as an overarching, multidimensional concept. These findings highlight the need for clearer conceptual boundaries, standardised measurement, and longitudinal and experimental research. PROSPERO CRD420251038303.

items.title: Public-Sector AI Adoption Toolkit
items.abstract: A practical, vendor-neutral toolkit for public institutions that want employees to use generative AI tools in everyday written work while protecting institutional information and keeping a person accountable for every official product. It is designed for document-intensive teams such as internal control, internal audit, oversight, legal support, procurement, and program administration. The toolkit has five parts that can be used separately or together: Risk Classification Worksheet: four classes of AI use, from low risk to prohibited, with a step-by-step classification guide and a use register. Human-Review Protocol: de-identification and redaction before AI use, structured instructions with the PACTO method, a technical review checklist, validation and signature, and specialized assistants for repetitive processes. Role-Based Curriculum Outline: a twelve-hour course in three sessions with step-by-step hands-on practice. Pilot Measurement Template: baselines defined in advance and reports that keep observations separate from causal conclusions. Facilitator Guide: preparing internal staff to deliver later cohorts. The toolkit systematizes practices the author developed in Brazilian public administration from 2024 to 2026, described in Gomes (2026), arXiv:2606.01517.

items.title: Quantum Haar Wavelet Transform methods applications and hardware realizations in quantum computing
items.abstract: Abstract Quantum Haar Wavelet Transform (QHWT) methods connect multiresolution analysis with quantum information processing through reversible averaging and differencing operations that can be implemented with comparatively compact circuits. Their localized basis functions, real-valued binary structure, and compatibility with hierarchical state representations make them attractive for resource-constrained quantum processing. Nevertheless, claims of practical superiority are difficult to generalize because published studies use heterogeneous encodings, simulators, hardware platforms, noise models, and evaluation metrics. This systematic review examines scholarly work on Haar-based quantum methods published between 1997 and March 2025. A PRISMA-oriented protocol was used to search major engineering and computing databases, remove duplicates, screen records, assess eligibility, and construct a qualitative evidence corpus. The review includes peer-reviewed journal and conference studies together with a limited number of historically influential technical reports and preprints; therefore, the corpus is described as scholarly literature rather than as a uniformly peer-reviewed dataset. Because the reported experiments are not sufficiently homogeneous for statistical pooling, numerical results are treated as study-specific evidence rather than global averages. The review makes three analytical contributions. First, it introduces a unified conceptual framework that links mathematical foundations, circuit realization, application design, hardware evaluation, and research translation. Second, it develops a taxonomy spanning transform theory, quantum image and signal processing, hardware implementation, and emerging quantum artificial intelligence and security applications. Third, it critically compares QHWT with Quantum Fourier Transform and higher-order wavelet approaches by distinguishing circuit depth, gate complexity, approximation behavior, hardware assumptions, and empirical validation. The synthesis indicates that QHWT is most compelling when localization, reversible multiresolution processing, and shallow circuit structure are more important than smooth-basis approximation. Individual studies report promising compression, feature-extraction, and hardware-efficiency results, but these findings remain conditional on encoding choices and platform constraints. Important limitations include sparse cross-platform benchmarking, limited fault-tolerant analysis, noise sensitivity, uncertain scaling, and optimization difficulties in variational quantum learning, including barren plateaus. items.title: Quen é quen na enfermaría lucense. O Espírito do Practicante en Medicina e Cirurxía, na vivencia da Enfermaría actual. Jesús Lamela Escobar.
items.abstract: This text presents the personal and professional career of Jesús “Suso” Lamela Escobar, a nurse from Lugo who recently retired after 46 years of professional practice in the Galician Health Service. Although he was never formally qualified as a practicante, his figure embodies the social meaning that this term still holds in rural Galicia: a healthcare professional with scientific knowledge, a strong vocation for service, closeness to the community and personal kindness. Born in Rosindo, Castroverde, in the mid-1950s, Jesús Lamela grew up in a family closely linked to healthcare, with a grandfather who was a physician and a father who was a practicante. This family tradition strongly influenced his professional choice. He studied at the School of Technical Health Assistants in Santiago de Compostela between 1975 and 1978, later completed his university diploma in Nursing and obtained the occupational health nursing qualification, formerly known as Company ATS. His professional career began in 1978 in A Pastoriza, where he worked for 20 years as a district ATS and home public healthcare practitioner. In 1998, he joined the Fingoi Health Centre, where he worked for another 26 years and eventually became its coordinator. Throughout his career, he was recognised for his professionalism, problem-solving skills, approachable character and commitment to colleagues, students and the people under his care. One of the areas he most enjoyed was minor surgery, together with the opportunity to help people directly. He also contributed to the clinical training of nursing students in Lugo. The text highlights his humanistic view of nursing, his confidence in the future of the profession and his belief that personal care will remain essential, even in a context increasingly shaped by new technologies and artificial intelligence. The profile concludes with a deeply vocational reflection: Jesús Lamela feels fully satisfied with the profession he chose and states that, if he could go back, he would become a nurse again. His greatest memory is having had the opportunity to help many people throughout his working life.

items.title: Queuing Theory as the Interpretable Core of Adaptive Hospital Operations: A Theory-Building Synthesis and the LASI Framework
items.abstract: Hospital patient flow and resource allocation are problems of decision-making under stochastic, non-stationary demand in a complex adaptive system, yet analytical queuing models, simulation, and artificial intelligence (AI) are treated as competing techniques, and no theory specifies how an interpretable core could safely constrain an adaptive one. This paper makes a theory-building contribution. It formalizes hospital operations as a single controlled-stochastic-process problem — defending that abstraction against network-optimization, partially-observable, cyber-physical, and decentralized alternatives — of which the analytical, simulation, and learning paradigms are three approximation strategies. From four functional requirements it derives the LASI framework (Layered Analytical–Simulation–Intelligence), argues each layer’s indispensability and the necessity of their dependency ordering, and specifies the core mechanism as a constrained-Markov-decision-process safety filter. Its most developed contribution is the validity-region mechanism: the analytical core may bound learning only where the core is validated, with the boundary estimated continuously by simulation through an analytical–reality divergence measure, and authority transferring between the analytical and simulation layers by a hysteresis rule. Governance is elevated from a passive gate to an active supervisory controller that resolves inter-layer conflicts and sets a responsible decision weight — the delegable authority to learning that keeps violation risk below a governance tolerance. Seven falsifiable propositions with boundary conditions state the theory. The synthesis repositions queuing theory not as a stage superseded by AI but as the interpretable, auditable core of accountable adaptive hospital operations.

items.title: RC-PRE-GHR: A Reality-Constrained Multi-Agent Survival Framework Under Energy, Trust, and Entropy Phase Transitions
items.abstract: A reality-constrained multi-agent framework modeling system survival under joint constraints of energy, trust, and entropy. We show that system stability undergoes sharp threshold transitions governed by a coupled entropy-trust-energy collapse mechanism. The Noah's Ark Condition defines the minimal sufficient structure for multi-agent survivability. Key contributions: - Unified trust-energy-entropy dynamical system - Formal collapse function with early-warning capability (detects 89%-100% of imminent failures 110-190 steps in advance) - Bounded stability manifold Omega - Measured thresholds: sigma* ~ 2.8 (process noise), E0* ~ 110-120 (energy budget) VERSION 2 NOTE (2026-10-02): This version replaces v1 with a corrected, fully reproducible package. The v1 simulation script did not implement the model described in the v1 manuscript, and its reported numbers could not be reproduced. In v2 the model definition was corrected in five documented ways (approach-alignment trust signal with finite interaction range; trust-gated energy-throttled cohesion policy; row-normalized trust entropy; metabolic cost delta = 0.2; energy clamped to R_+), and ALL reported figures and numbers now regenerate end-to-end from the deposited script rc_pre_ghr_faithful.py (numpy + matplotlib only). Revised thresholds supersede the v1 values (v1: sigma* ~ 0.2, E0* ~ 100; v2: sigma* ~ 2.8, E0* ~ 110-120). See Appendix B of the revised manuscript for the full correction list. items.title: Recent advances and challenges in electronic nose technology for agricultural commodities and food quality assessment
items.abstract: Traditional methods for analyzing agricultural produce and food quality, such as chromatography and sensory evaluation, are often expensive, time consuming, and require skilled professionals, making them hard to implement for rapid and large-scale testing. The advent of Electronic nose (E-Nose) technology presents a promising alternative by emulating the human olfactory system through sensor arrays that identify volatile compounds and produce distinctive response patterns. This review examines the principles, evolution, and applications of E-nose systems for assessing the quality of food and agricultural products across diverse categories, including fish, meat, dairy products, tea, coffee, and edible oils. These systems provide non-destructive and smart analytical solutions for modern food-processing industries. Their role in identifying contamination, freshness assessment, authenticity, and monitoring fermentation plays a crucial role in modern food processing. Recent advancements integrating artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methodologies have significantly enhanced the efficacy of E-nose systems, enabling superior pattern recognition, data interpretation, and precise prediction capabilities. This enables objective and accurate quality assessment. Despite these advantages, the widespread adoption of this technology is hindered due to sensor drift, low sensitivity, high initial costs, and the difficulty of processing such complex data. Future research should focus on enhancing sensor stability, formulating resilient data analytics models, and decreasing system costs to facilitate scalability. Overall, E-nose technology has potential to transform food-quality assessment by providing the food industry with rapid, non-destructive, and intelligent analytical methods.
